config.grain_rationale: One record is one charity as registered with the ACNC, i.e. one legal entity holding charity registration. The address columns are the charity's contact address, not a site or premises record, and the operational and purpose flag columns are attributes of that same registered entity. Record identity is therefore the entity.

record_id.rationale: ABN was tried first but the full register contains 6 holdout records that collide on ABN: the register includes related/sub-entity rows and rows with no ABN, so ABN is not a unique per-record key across the whole file even though it looked unique in discovery (477 of 477 distinct in 480 rows). content_hash is used instead so every distinct row gets a traceable, stable id without inventing uniqueness. ABN remains mapped as entity.abn where present.

fields.rationale: Column labelled ABN; 477/477 present values are 11 digits with a valid ABN checksum (abn_checksum_valid_rate 1.0), and 0 errors on holdout. Canonical Australian business identifier. Note the same ABN can appear on more than one row, so it is not used as the record id.

Column is explicitly Charity_Legal_Name and the publisher states the register presents the formal legal name. Scope current_legal_name. Held-out values carry legal-form suffixes (Incorporated, 'The Trustee for ...', 'P&C Association'), consistent with registered names rather than display names. The source gives no start date for the name itself, so no valid_from_path; Registration_Date is deliberately not attached to the name.

Publisher evidence states the effective registration date is the date with ACNC, explicitly distinguished from the organisation's original establishment. 476/480 discovery values and 1179/1179 holdout values match dd/mm/yyyy (0 errors). The date is when ACNC charity registration became true, hence scope charity_registration and valid_from_path on this claim.

Column is the charity's website; values are bare domains (www.x.org.au) or http(s) URLs. The website op rejects malformed values. One holdout value is prose containing two URLs and a parenthetical ('HTTPS://... AND WWW... (WWWW...)') rather than a single URL; rejecting that is the correct outcome, since coercing it would emit a broken URL as the entity's canonical website.

Three free-text street lines of the charity's contact address, joined with a single space so multi-line addresses cannot concatenate without a separator; lines 2 and 3 are almost always null so the separator rarely appears. Publisher evidence says the address is contact information, hence scope entity_contact_address. Caveat a reviewer should know: Address_Line_1 often holds a venue/premises or building descriptor rather than a street line (e.g. 'Pembroke School', 'St Christopher's Pastoral Centre', 'Egan Park', 'Community Centre') alongside true street addresses, and some values are PO boxes. The source does not distinguish a licensed/operating premises address from the entity's contact address, so this is mapped as contact_address and not as a premises address; downstream users should not treat address.full as a verified street address.

Town_City is the suburb/locality of the contact address; 362 distinct discovery values and all 1061 holdout values read as Australian localities ('Dubbo', 'Altona North', 'DONNYBROOK'), published case preserved as no canonical casing rule exists.

State column holds AU state/territory abbreviations; holdout includes a trailing-whitespace value ('SA ') which trim then state resolves to SA. state sends anything unrecognised to OTHER rather than guessing. 0 errors on holdout.

Postcode is the contact address postcode; the postcode op validates 4-digit AU codes and re-pads 3-digit NT codes. The column is free text and carries occasional junk rather than just formatting noise: holdout rejects were '80571' (5 digits) and 'Cloverdale' (a locality name entered in the postcode field), plus one 6-digit value in discovery. Rejecting these is correct behaviour because coercing a locality name or a 5-digit string into address.postcode would assert a postcode the source never stated; the loss is a fraction of a percent of rows.

Country of the contact address. Discovery shows only 'Australia' in mixed case plus one 'Singapore'. The previous passthrough behaviour asserted any unrecognised string as a canonical country, which turned a publisher typo ('Austria' on an Altona North VIC contact address) into a false country claim. passthrough is now false: only explicitly recognised values are emitted (Australian spellings -> AU, Singapore -> SG because the source genuinely states it) and anything else is left unmapped rather than asserted. Residual uncertainty: an unlisted genuine overseas country would be dropped rather than emitted.

unmapped.reason: The critic suggested a filtered emission to entity.trading_name, and some holdout values do look like public names ('Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc.', 'Walker Close Community Centre'). I am still leaving it unmapped. Publisher evidence states this column is the names the charity is publicly known by and explicitly does NOT classify every alternate name as a trading name, so emitting trading_name would assert a trading use the source does not establish. The column is also irreducibly heterogeneous: person names ('Shannon Schedlich'), fragments ('Admin', 'NSP'), legal-form-tweaked duplicates of the legal name itself ('Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc.' vs 'Donnybrook Mens Shed Incorporated' - a spelling variant, not a trading name), and trust-entity wrappers. A filter cannot separate spelling variants from genuine trading names without guesswork. If this is wanted downstream it should be modelled as an alias/other-name field, not entity.trading_name.

Constant 'Business' on 480/480 rows; describes the category of the address record, not a canonical entity attribute. Address semantics are already carried by the address.* mappings, and mapping it to entity_type would be a guess.

Publisher evidence explicitly distinguishes the original establishment/incorporation date from the effective ACNC registration date, and the ontology has only entity.date_registered, so mapping this there would be wrong (the critic agrees). Flagged by the critic as an ontology gap: if entity.date_established is added it should map there. It is also not a validity start for the legal name.
ACNC size classification (Small/Medium/Large) is a regulatory reporting category, not an ontology field; there is no entity.size target and it is not entity_type.
Count of the charity's responsible persons (officers); an attribute of governance, not of the entity's identity, form or status. No ontology target.
Accounting period end (e.g. '30-Jun') is a reporting convention, not a date of the entity or of a claim in the ontology.

Presence flag for operating in a state. The ontology has address.state as the entity's address, which is a different assertion; mapping an operating-in-jurisdiction flag to address.state would falsely claim the charity is located there. No ontology target for operational footprint.

config.notes: REVISION after holdout review. Changes: (1) record_id switched from columns[ABN] to content_hash - the error was real, 6 holdout rows collide on ABN because the register contains related/sub-entity rows and rows lacking an ABN. (2) address.country passthrough disabled - the previous passthrough emitted a typo ('Austria' on an Altona North VIC address) as an asserted canonical country; now only explicitly recognised values emit (AU, and SG for the Singapore rows actually present). (3) Rejected WEBSITE_INVALID and POSTCODE_INVALID values are intentional rejections of malformed prose / locality-names-in-postcode, not parser bugs; documented in their rationales. (4) address.full confidence lowered to 0.72 and its rationale now warns that the first line is often a venue/premises or PO box descriptor rather than a street address. (5) Other_Organisation_Names remains unmapped despite the critic's 'missed' suggestion: publisher evidence warns alternate names are not attested trading names, and the column mixes spelling variants of the legal name with person names and fragments, so a filter would require guesswork; the correct model is an alias field. (6) Date_Organisation_Established is a genuine ontology gap (no entity.date_established). No entity.status or entity.entity_type mapping was added: the register has no deregistered/in-liquidation or business-form column, so both stay unasserted rather than guessed.

config.notes: REVISION after holdout review. Changes: (1) record_id switched from columns[ABN] to content_hash - the error was real, 6 holdout rows collide on ABN because the register contains related/sub-entity rows and rows lacking an ABN. (2) address.country passthrough disabled - the previous passthrough emitted a typo ('Austria' on an Altona North VIC address) as an asserted canonical country; now only explicitly recognised values emit (AU, and SG for the Singapore rows actually present). (3) Rejected WEBSITE_INVALID and POSTCODE_INVALID values are intentional rejections of malformed prose / locality-names-in-postcode, not parser bugs; documented in their rationales. (4) address.full confidence lowered to 0.72 and its rationale now warns that the first line is often a venue/premises or PO box descriptor rather than a street address. (5) Other_Organisation_Names remains unmapped despite the critic's 'missed' suggestion: publisher evidence warns alternate names are not attested trading names, and the column mixes spelling variants of the legal name with person names and fragments, so a filter would require guesswork; the correct model is an alias field. (6) Date_Organisation_Established is a genuine ontology gap (no entity.date_established). No entity.status or entity.entity_type mapping was added: the register has no deregistered/in-liquidation or business-form column, so both stay unasserted rather than guessed.

config.grain_rationale: Each row is one name-history record for an ASIC-registered legal entity, identified by its ACN. ASIC joins changed names onto the same registration: exactly one row per entity carries Current Name Indicator=Y and holds the entity's current registered name, while the other rows hold former names and carry the current name in the separate Current Name column. All entity attributes mapped here (ACN, ABN, entity type, status, registration date) are attributes of the legal person, not of the row's name; the name rules are gated so current and former names are never confused.

record_id.rationale: ACN is stable per legal entity but repeats across name-history rows (471 distinct in 473 discovery rows; holdout shows the same pattern), so ACN alone is not unique per record. ACN+Company Name+Current Name Indicator identifies one name row of one entity uniquely; Current Name Indicator is included so a repeated name for the same ACN cannot collide.

fields.rationale: Publisher word-for-word: Company Name is the current registered company name when Current Name Indicator is Y. The gate is essential - without it every superseded name was emitted as a current_legal_name claim (the critic caught LOVINI HOLDINGS PTY LTD presented as current alongside MONAKA PTY LTD). Gated: 301/473 discovery rows, every entity gets exactly one current name. ASIC holds legal names only, so entity.legal_name, not trading_name. Column is space-padded to fixed width, hence collapse_whitespace then trim.

Complementary branch: rows without the Y indicator are name-history rows, so Company Name there is a superseded registered name of the same ACN - a former legal name, not a current one. Gated: 172/473 discovery rows, exactly the complement of the current-name rows, so every name row is classified as current or former and none is dropped. valid_to left empty because the publisher states the extract does not establish when each former name stopped being valid, and a current name's start date does not establish the end date of a previous name.

Corrected direction. The critic established that on a history row Current Name holds the entity's CURRENT registered name (record 1 Company Name=LOVINI with Current Name=MONAKA; record 2 the current-name row for the same ACN with Company Name=MONAKA), so this is a current_legal_name claim, not a former alias. Current Name Start Date dates that current name, so it is valid_from for this claim. Not gated on the indicator because the columns are complementary (301 indicator rows vs 172 populated Current Name rows), so this supplies current names for entities whose current name is expressed this way. It repeats a name the Y-gated rule also emits for the same ACN, which is a consistent duplicate assertion rather than a conflict.

Profile: 100% of discovery values match ^\d{9}$ and pass the ACN checksum (1.0 rate); 471 distinct over 473 rows, consistent with one entity spanning several name rows. Holdout: 1163/1163 emitted, zero errors. ASIC's primary company identifier, so it is the business identifier, not the row's own ID.

Publisher: ABN 0 is a missing value. Profile: 145/473 discovery rows hold the literal single-character '0'; the other 328 are 11 digits and all pass the ABN checksum (0.693 valid rate is exactly the non-zero share). null_if '0' then the checksummed abn transform, which also strips zero padding that would otherwise fail the checksum. Holdout: 844/1163 emitted, zero errors.

Publisher: REGD=registered, DRGD=deregistered, EXAD covers BOTH receivership and liquidation, SOFF=strike-off action in progress. This is the entity's own registration status, so entity.status is the correct target. REGD->active and DRGD->deregistered are direct. EXAD now maps to unknown instead of in_liquidation: the critic is right that inferring liquidation from a code that also covers receivership would mislabel every receiver, and unknown is the enum's honest value. SOFF is a pending strike-off, neither suspended nor deregistered, so also unknown.
Publisher: Date of Registration is a company event with day-first dates. All shapes are 99/99/9999 and holdout values parse day-first correctly (08/01/1990 -> 1990-01-08, 03/04/1935 -> 1935-04-03).

Accepted the critic's missed item: APTY (proprietary) and APUB (public) both denote an ASIC-registered company body, which is precisely the ontology value 'company'. This is the source's own statement of business form rather than a default, so mapping it is preferable to leaving entity_type unknown and losing the only explicit evidence. The proprietary/public distinction has no enum value, so both collapse to company; any unseen code falls to unknown.

unmapped.reason: LMSH (limited by shares) and LMGT (limited by guarantee) are ASIC share/guarantee classes - capital structure, not business form. Type already establishes entity_type=company from evidence, and mapping Class would add no distinct enum value while risking misrepresentation of limited-by-guarantee bodies, so it is recorded here as supporting context only.
PROP, PSTC, LISN, LIST, ULSN, ULST etc. describe company sub-class/share structure. No ontology target and no additional defensible entity_type information beyond Type.

Publisher: this is the historical jurisdiction in which the entity was previously registered, not the entity's current address. The ontology offers only address fields, and address.state would assert a current location the source does not establish. A previous state of registration is a historical jurisdiction, so it stays unmapped.

A state-level registration number, not an ACN, ABN or NZBN, and the ontology has no target for it. Numeric extraction would risk being mistaken for an entity identifier. Also space-padded (trailing blanks in several values).
Present rate 0.0 - the column is entirely empty in this extract, so no content evidence exists. It is in any case a report-processing flag, not an entity attribute.

Not an entity attribute itself - it is the row-level discriminator between current and former name rows, so it is used as the 'when' gate on the two Company Name rules and in record_id rather than emitted as a field.

Kept off observation.valid_to because a deregistration date ends the entity's existence, not the validity of its name/ACN/address claims, and the publisher treats it as a separate company event. It is also too sparse to serve as a bound (19 populated rows vs 28 DRGD rows). The ontology has no event-date target for it, so it is unmapped rather than forced into valid_to; the DRGD status code already carries the fact that the entity is deregistered.

config.notes: Revised after critic review. Key fixes: (1) Company Name is now split into two complementary gated rules so a superseded name is never emitted as current_legal_name; (2) Current Name is reclassified as current_legal_name (not former_legal_name) with Current Name Start Date as valid_from, correcting the inverted semantics; (3) EXAD and SOFF now map to unknown instead of guessing in_liquidation; (4) Type added as entity.entity_type=company per the critic's missed-item suggestion. Current Name Indicator is deliberately not emitted as a field but used as the gate and in record_id. The Current Name rule intentionally duplicates the current name for ACNs whose current-name row is expressed in the other column - these are consistent assertions, not conflicts. Previous State of Registration is deliberately left unmapped: it is a historical jurisdiction, not a current address.

Gated: 172/473 discovery rows, exactly the complement of the current-name rows, so every name row is classified as current or former and none is dropped. valid_to left empty because the publisher states the extract does not establish when each former name stopped being valid, and a current name's start date does not establish the end date of a previous name.

Corrected direction. The critic established that on a history row Current Name holds the entity's CURRENT registered name (record 1 Company Name=LOVINI with Current Name=MONAKA; record 2 the current-name row for the same ACN with Company Name=MONAKA), so this is a current_legal_name claim, not a former alias. Current Name Start Date dates that current name, so it is valid_from for this claim. Not gated on the indicator because the columns are complementary (301 indicator rows vs 172 populated Current Name rows), so this supplies current names for entities whose current name is expressed this way. It repeats a name the Y-gated rule also emits for the same ACN, which is a consistent duplicate assertion rather than a conflict.

Profile: 100% of discovery values match ^\d{9}$ and pass the ACN checksum (1.0 rate); 471 distinct over 473 rows, consistent with one entity spanning several name rows. Holdout: 1163/1163 emitted, zero errors. ASIC's primary company identifier, so it is the business identifier, not the row's own ID.

Publisher: ABN 0 is a missing value. Profile: 145/473 discovery rows hold the literal single-character '0'; the other 328 are 11 digits and all pass the ABN checksum (0.693 valid rate is exactly the non-zero share). null_if '0' then the checksummed abn transform, which also strips zero padding that would otherwise fail the checksum. Holdout: 844/1163 emitted, zero errors.

Publisher: REGD=registered, DRGD=deregistered, EXAD covers BOTH receivership and liquidation, SOFF=strike-off action in progress. This is the entity's own registration status, so entity.status is the correct target. REGD->active and DRGD->deregistered are direct. EXAD now maps to unknown instead of in_liquidation: the critic is right that inferring liquidation from a code that also covers receivership would mislabel every receiver, and unknown is the enum's honest value. SOFF is a pending strike-off, neither suspended nor deregistered, so also unknown.
Publisher: Date of Registration is a company event with day-first dates. All shapes are 99/99/9999 and holdout values parse day-first correctly (08/01/1990 -> 1990-01-08, 03/04/1935 -> 1935-04-03).

Accepted the critic's missed item: APTY (proprietary) and APUB (public) both denote an ASIC-registered company body, which is precisely the ontology value 'company'. This is the source's own statement of business form rather than a default, so mapping it is preferable to leaving entity_type unknown and losing the only explicit evidence. The proprietary/public distinction has no enum value, so both collapse to company; any unseen code falls to unknown.
ASIC Class code (LMSH, LMGT) is the publisher's capital-structure class; kept as publisher term.
ASIC Sub Class code (PROP, PSTC, LISN) is the publisher's subclass code; kept raw.
Data dictionary: historical jurisdiction of registration; carries no address evidence.
Day-first deregistration event date; blank means still registered, so left missing rather than zero.

unmapped.reason: A state-level registration number, not an ACN, ABN or NZBN, and the ontology has no target for it. Numeric extraction would risk being mistaken for an entity identifier. Also space-padded (trailing blanks in several values).
Present rate 0.0 - the column is entirely empty in this extract, so no content evidence exists. It is in any case a report-processing flag, not an entity attribute.

Not an entity attribute itself - it is the row-level discriminator between current and former name rows, so it is used as the 'when' gate on the two Company Name rules and in record_id rather than emitted as a field.

config.notes: Revised after critic review. Key fixes: (1) Company Name is now split into two complementary gated rules so a superseded name is never emitted as current_legal_name; (2) Current Name is reclassified as current_legal_name (not former_legal_name) with Current Name Start Date as valid_from, correcting the inverted semantics; (3) EXAD and SOFF now map to unknown instead of guessing in_liquidation; (4) Type added as entity.entity_type=company per the critic's missed-item suggestion. Current Name Indicator is deliberately not emitted as a field but used as the gate and in record_id. The Current Name rule intentionally duplicates the current name for ACNs whose current-name row is expressed in the other column - these are consistent assertions, not conflicts. Previous State of Registration is deliberately left unmapped: it is a historical jurisdiction, not a current address.

mappings.title: QBCC Licensed Contractors Register
mappings.resource: QBCC register of licensed builders and contractors

config.grain_rationale: Each record is one QBCC licence held by a licensee (Licence Number + Licence Grade + Licence Class Type identify the licence; _id is the CKAN row id). The business participant is the licensee named in 'Licensee Name'. Licence-level attributes (grade, class, financial category) describe the licence, not the entity. The register is a flat export that never distinguishes a registered legal name from a trading name, so 'Licensee Name' is mapped only to entity.legal_name: for 'Company' rows it is the registered company name (corroborated by a checksum-valid ACN and PTY LTD suffixes), for 'Individual' rows it is the natural person who is the licensee. No trading name is claimed because the source provides none.

record_id.rationale: CKAN datastore row id; 508/508 distinct across the discovery partition and unique in held-out validation, so it identifies the licence record. Licence Number is not unique (506 distinct vs 508 rows), so it cannot be used alone.

fields.rationale: Single licensee-name column in a government licence register, mapped in full with no suffix heuristic and no suppression. Previous revision emitted only company-suffixed names here (7% coverage) and pushed personal names to trading_name; the reviewer rejected that split. An individual licensee is the natural person holding the licence, so its name belongs in legal_name rather than being dropped or relabelled as a trading name.

Direct source column in '99 999 999 999' shape; ABN checksum valid on 99.6% of discovery rows and 99.0% of held-out rows (1 and 6 rejections respectively). The abn transform strips separators and refuses to emit a checksum-invalid value, so bad source data surfaces as a counted error instead of a fabricated ABN. The residual ~1% rejections are reported honestly, not hidden.
All present values are '999 999 999'; 100% ACN checksum-valid in both discovery (34/34) and held-out (76/76) with zero errors. ACN is never derived from the ABN.

The source states the licensee type directly and 'C' -> company is well supported (ACN present, PTY LTD names). 'I' is deliberately NOT mapped to sole_trader after the reviewer rejected that inference (an individual licensee may be a partner or trust principal); 'I' rows therefore resolve to the ontology default 'unknown' rather than a guess.
Free-text single-line business address ending in state + postcode, e.g. '15 radiata pl Peregian Springs QLD 4573'. Passed through as stated by the source with whitespace normalisation only.

All addresses follow '<street> <suburb> <STATE> <postcode>'; the state token immediately before the trailing postcode is extracted and normalised by the state op (unknown -> OTHER). Reviewer verdict 'ok'; 1080/1092 held-out rows emitted with zero errors.
Trailing numeric token of the address, validated by the postcode op (AU 4-digit, NT re-pad). Reviewer verdict 'ok'; 100% coverage with zero errors in both partitions.

constants.rationale: Queensland Building and Construction Commission register; every address carries a QLD state code and an AU 4-digit postcode. Inferred from the publisher and address format rather than a source column, so confidence is moderate and flagged for review.

unmapped.reason: CKAN datastore row id for the licence record, not a business identifier; used only as record_id.
Identifier of the licence/permit, not of the business. Also not unique per record (506 distinct for 508 rows). Not mapped onto any entity field and not used to derive an ACN.

Only address.full, address.state and address.postcode are taken from this column. address.locality is deliberately not mapped: the reviewer found the street-type-suffix heuristic brittle (missed COURT, ESPLANADE, unit-numbered and street-less addresses) and it covered only ~58-60% of held-out rows. Emitting no locality leaves the value absent rather than wrong.
Human-readable form of Licence Type CODE ('Individual'/'Company'); CODE is the machine value used for entity_type, so this is deduplicated to avoid two observations of one logical field.
Licence financial category ('Self Certification - Trade' for 100% of discovery rows), a property of the licence, not of the entity.
Code form of the licence financial category ('SCT1'); licence attribute, single-valued in the discovery partition, not an entity field.

QBCC licence grade (Trade Contractor Licence, Site Supervisor, Fire Occupational, ...). A licence attribute, not an ANZSIC or industry classification of the business, so not mapped to entity.industry_code.

Trade/occupation class of the licence (Carpentry, Plumbing and Drainage, ...). It is the nearest industry signal in the source, but it is a licence scope category and not ANZSIC, while entity.industry_code is documented as 'ANZSIC where available'. Recording a QBCC trade class there would place a non-conforming code in an ANZSIC-typed field; it is left unmapped and reported as a coverage gap instead.

Fixes for the reviewer's verdicts: (1) entity.trading_name REMOVED ('wrong' verdict - a personal licensee name is not a trading name, and for companies it duplicated the legal name); (2) the suffix-based legal_name heuristic REMOVED - 'Licensee Name' is now mapped in full to entity.legal_name (coverage 100%, no suppression, no guessing), which also resolves the 'doubtful' over-suppression of individual licensees; (3) entity.entity_type now maps only 'C'->company and lets 'I' fall to the ontology default 'unknown', removing the rejected 'I'->sole_trader inference; (4) address.locality REMOVED as brittle ('doubtful'), so address output is full/state/postcode only, all of which the reviewer rated 'ok'. Retained deliberately: entity.abn and entity.acn (direct, checksum-validated source columns rated 'ok'; ABN keeps a reported ~1% checksum rejection rather than hiding it) and address.country 'AU' at reduced confidence 0.8 and flagged. config.grain_rationale: One record is one current Australian credit licence, identified by CRED_LIC_NUM, held by a legal person named in CRED_LIC_NAME (ASIC issues credit licences to legal entities). The business attributes mapped are those of the licensee/holder; the licence number, licence start date and licence status are attributes of the licence, not of the entity, so they are not mapped as business identifiers or entity.status.

record_id.rationale: CRED_LIC_NUM has present_rate 1.0 and 464 distinct values across 464 discovery records, i.e. unique per licence record; it is the natural traceable key for the licence grain.

fields.rationale: Column is CRED_LIC_NAME on a credit licence register: the licence is issued to the named holder, and the publisher states licence names follow the business register. Values are registered-form names ('...PTY LTD', 'LIMITED'). Some holders are individuals (e.g. 'TAN, JINTANG'), expected for sole-trader licensees; the field remains the registered legal name of the licensee, not a trading name.

CRED_LIC_BN is the licence's business name field, present on 34.5% of rows; values are short trading brands ('DISCOVERY FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT', 'STACKS FINANCE', 'PLANNING PARTNERS') distinct from the registered names in CRED_LIC_NAME. Business/brand names map to trading_name.

Combined ABN/ACN column: 420 of 464 discovery values are 11-digit checksum-valid ABNs. The regex_extract step restricts this rule to the 11-digit branch so the abn transform only ever sees ABN-shaped values; ACN-shaped, 7-8 digit and placeholder values produce no ABN observation instead of an error.

27 of 464 records carry a 9-digit ACN-shaped value in CRED_LIC_ABN_ACN; that branch is an ACN (the last 9 digits of an ABN are not always an ACN, so it is validated with the acn checksum, never derived). The regex_extract step selects only 9-digit values, so 11-digit ABNs, 7-8 digit values and the placeholder '0' are excluded from this field rather than erroring.
ASIC credit licensee extracts carry the licensee's locality/state/postcode as a group with latitude/longitude, i.e. the holder's contact address on the licence record.
All 464 values are already 2-3 letter AU state abbreviations over 8 distinct values (NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, ACT, ...), consistent with the state enum.
All 464 values have shape 9999 (4-digit AU postcodes, e.g. 2000, 3000, 6102); normalised with the postcode transform.

constants.rationale: ASIC Australian credit licence register covering Australian licensees; all observed states are AU jurisdictions.

unmapped.reason: Constant register label ('Credit Licence') for every row; carries no entity attribute.
Identifier of the licence record, not of the business. Used only as record_id; the ontology has no licence field.

Date the credit licence started, not the entity's registration date (publisher evidence: grant/suspension/cancellation dates concern the licence). Mapping it to entity.date_registered would misstate company registration.
Dataset is 'Current' and the column is empty in every discovery row; also concerns licence end, not entity validity.
Status of the licence (single value 'APPR' = approved), not of the legal entity; licence status is not entity.status.
Free-text licence-condition contravention history (present on 0.2% of rows); describes the licence, not the entity.
Australian Financial Services licence number of the licensee, a licence identifier with no ontology target; 91.6% of values are the placeholder '0' anyway.
Latitude coordinate with no ontology address field for coordinates.
Longitude coordinate with no ontology address field for coordinates.
External dispute resolution scheme membership(s) of the licensee ('AFCA~FOS'); a compliance attribute, not an entity or address field.
Free-text description of what the licence authorises; describes licence scope, not the entity.

config.notes: Licence-grain register: record_id is the licence number, and licence dates/status are deliberately not mapped to entity fields. CRED_LIC_ABN_ACN is a mixed column - 420/464 are checksum-valid 11-digit ABNs, 27 are 9-digit ACN-shaped, 13 are the placeholder '0', and a few are 7-8 digits; each identifier rule is shape-guarded with regex_extract so the checksummed transforms only see values of the right length and invalid values yield no observation rather than an error. entity_type is left unmapped because no column states the business form explicitly (names ending in PTY LTD are not treated as a stated type). Address fields are the licensee's contact details on the licence record; the geography of the register does not by itself prove each record's location, but locality/state/postcode plus coordinates are presented as the licensee's address.

mappings.title: Suitable Operator Register (SOR) for Environmentally Relevant Activities (ERAs)

config.grain_rationale: One record is one suitable-operator registration (identified by an RSO number) held by a corporation, government body, association or individual/sole trader. This is program participation, not the entity register itself; the holder's attributes (name, ACN/ABN, form, location) are mapped, while the registration status, RSO number and the program registration date are programme facts and stay unmapped.

record_id.rationale: RSO Number is the department-issued suitable-operator reference; distinct 459/459 across the discovery partition, so unique per registration (one row per registration).

fields.rationale: For explicit non-individual entity types the Customer Name is the registered style of the licence holder (e.g. '"OVER THE TOP" ROOF RESTORATIONS PTY. LTD'); licences are issued to legal persons, so this is the holder's legal name. Quote/asterisk characters retained as publisher text.

Values are 'ACN nnnnnnnnn'; 237/249 present values are 9-digit ACNs and 96% of present values pass the ACN checksum. The prefix-anchored regex requires the literal 'ACN' prefix so 'ABN ...' and 'ARBN ...' values are not misparsed. Values failing the checksum are reported as errors, never repaired.

A minority of Business Number values are prefixed 'ABN ' with 11 digits; the ABN checksum transform validates them. 'ACN' and 'ARBN' values are excluded by the prefix anchor, and no ACN is ever derived from an ABN.

Entity Type explicitly states the business form. 'Local Government Authority' added as government (heldout showed Allconnex Water under this label). 'Government Owned Corporation' -> government, following the source's own 'Government' wording, though it is legally a company; low-stakes either way. 'An individual or Sole trader' is a combined label that cannot distinguish a person from a business form, so it falls to the default 'unknown' rather than a guessed sole_trader.

Location is 'SUBURB, STATE, POSTCODE' (e.g. 'South Brisbane, QLD, 4101'); the first comma-delimited component is the suburb/locality. Scope is ambiguous (holder contact address vs licensed premises) and is flagged in notes.

Second comma-delimited component is the state abbreviation (QLD dominant, plus VIC/NSW/WA and NT/SA/TAS/ACT); normalised with the state transform. Rows whose separator shape defeats extraction stay null rather than being guessed.
Trailing comma-delimited component is the postcode; some raw values are 3/2/1 digits, and the postcode transform re-pads 3-digit NT codes.

constants.rationale: Queensland environment department register; all locations are AU suburbs/states, with a minority of holders located interstate (VIC, NSW, WA).

unmapped.reason: Status of the suitable-operator registration (a permit), not of the legal entity; only value present is 'Registered'. Mapping it to entity.status would misstate the entity's status.
Department-assigned suitable-operator reference for the registration; used as record_id. It identifies the permit, not the business.

Per publisher documentation this is the date the holder was registered as a suitable operator (programme participation), not the entity's incorporation/company registration date, and the claim_scope catalogue has no programme-registration scope. Mapping it to entity.date_registered would assert a legal-entity registration date the source does not support.

unmapped.source_path: Customer Name (Entity Type = 'An individual or Sole trader')
unmapped.reason: For these rows Customer Name is a natural person's name (e.g. 'WILLIAM YOUNG'). Nothing in the source establishes it as a registered business/trading name, and the combined label cannot establish a business form; the ontology has no target for an individual's name, so it is not emitted.

'ARBN nnnnnnnnn' is an Australian Registered Body Number, issued to a foreign registered body; it is neither an ACN nor an ABN, so those rows yield no entity.acn/abn and must not be mistaken for missing identifiers.

config.notes: Programme register: each row is a suitable-operator registration (RSO number) held by a corporation, government body, association or an individual/sole trader. Registration Status, RSO Number and Registration Date describe the registration, not the entity, so they are unmapped. Customer Name is asserted as legal name only for explicit non-individual entity types; natural-person names under the combined 'An individual or Sole trader' label are not emitted. Business Number mixes ACN-, ABN- and ARBN-prefixed values, handled by two prefix-anchored rules so neither a wrong-length ACN nor an ABN-derived ACN is produced; a few values genuinely fail the ACN checksum and are reported as errors. Location 'SUBURB, STATE, POSTCODE' is split into locality/state/postcode because it is the only geographic evidence; its scope (holder contact vs licensed premises) is ambiguous, so it is emitted without a specific address claim_scope.
